answer.rationale: The competitor's entry pricing tempts a promotional response, but memory_73 explicitly records that promotional pricing materially reduced 30-day retention and warns against generalizing it — that directly conflicts with the sustainable long-term qualified revenue objective, so I decline it despite the situational pull. The two observed declines (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point at the funnel itself, and onboarding completion sits upstream of activation, so fixing it plausibly recovers both rather than one. I verify memory_86 (the direct basis for the chosen action, and the one whose effect size and population I most need to confirm) and memory_31 (adjacent signup-field evidence that would corroborate or undercut the same mechanism); I do not spend budget on memory_73 because verifying it could only strengthen a warning I am already honoring. Caveats I am carrying forward rather than resolving: memory_86 and memory_31 were consolidated on self-serve/SMB accounts and may not transfer to the segment the competitor is taking; both are 20-60 days stale and the current declines may have a cause the archived records never tested; and shortening onboarding can trade completion for downstream value if the removed steps carried setup that drives retention — a completion lift that does not convert into activation or retained revenue is the failure mode to watch. Hence a standard experiment with retention and activation as guardrail metrics, not a broad rollout. Activation messaging (memory_91) is the fallback if verification weakens the onboarding record; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) addresses neither declining metric this week.
